reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports that melt spinning refines grains and affects mechanical properties in a CoCrFeMnNi HEA, but it does not address MnNiSi-based alloys, magnetocaloric effects, annealing effects, or gradient microstructures. Thus, most key premises specific to the hypothesis are unsupported.
premises: Melt spinning produces a very fine-grained microstructure in alloys
Grain refinement via melt spinning improves mechanical properties
Controlled low-temperature annealing relieves residual stresses without significant grain growth
The magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based alloys is tied to a magnetostructural transition
A gradient microstructure (fine surface, coarser core) can be engineered by melt spinning and annealing
